explanations: drainEncoder takes the encoder lock first and then each channel lock, while assign takes the channel lock first and then the encoder lock. If assign(ch1, encA) holds ch1's lock and is waiting for encA's lock while drainEncoder(encA) holds encA's lock and is waiting for ch1's lock, neither can make progress. The Mutex has no timeout, so both calls hang forever, and every later operation on that channel or encoder (including updateRenditions) queues behind them. drainEncoder should acquire locks in the same channel-then-encoder order (for example snapshot the channel ids, then lock each channel and then the encoder), or use one global ordering rule.

Locks are per channel id (channelLock(id)). Only a call for chX contends with assign, which holds chX's mutex across the awaited persistAssignment. Other channels have their own Mutex instances, so they proceed. Single-threaded execution does not serialize async work across awaits, and Mutex.acquire waits rather than throwing.

release() shifts one waiter and calls its resolver without clearing locked, so ownership passes directly to the next waiter in FIFO order. locked only becomes false when no one is waiting. Nothing resolves all waiters, and the mutex does not track which context holds it.

The capacity check happens before persistAssignment, so nothing is written. The error propagates out of the inner runExclusive (whose finally releases the encoder lock) and then out of the outer one (whose finally releases the channel lock). No lock leaks, and the store is untouched.
